To do or say again (and again).

examples.text: The scientists repeated the experiment in order to confirm the result.
I'll tell you my secret, but first promise me you won't repeat it to anyone else!
I don't mind talking about the incident, but one gets tired of repeating themself after the hundredth time.

When this conversation was repeated in detail within the hearing of the young woman in question, and undoubtedly for his benefit, Mr. Trevor threw shame to the winds and scandalized the Misses Brewster then and there by proclaiming his father to have been a country storekeeper.

Let them repeat that now. Let them tell that to General McArthur and his men. Let them tell that to the sailors who today are hitting hard in the far waters of the Pacific. Let them tell that to the boys in the Flying Fortresses. Let them tell that to the Marines.

glosses: To refill (a prescription).
To happen again; recur.

examples.text: A day like that has not yet repeated itself.

glosses: To echo the words of (a person).

examples.text: Their rationale with repeating me was that the prior program had not been of sufficient quality to teach me the error of my ways.

glosses: To strike the hours, as a watch does.
To make trial of again; to undergo or encounter again.

examples.text: He[…] repeats the danger of the burning town.

glosses: To repay or refund (an excess received).

examples.text: Add 100, left 50. Repeat, over.

An iteration; a repetition.

examples.text: We gave up after the third repeat because it got boring.

glosses: A television program shown after its initial presentation; a rerun.
A refill of a prescription.

To play again.

examples.text: So I replayed my '46 scenario and asked another unstandard academic, a charismatic, disenchanted philosophy professor named George Geiger, who had been Lou Gehrig's backup on the Columbia baseball team and John Dewey's last graduate student, what I should do.

glosses: To display a recording of a previous event, especially multiple times.

examples.text: Sundown yellow moon / I replay the past / I know every scene by heart / They all went by so fast
It was a feeling so alien to his usual state of being that he was not able to put a name to it until that night, lying in bed and looking at the ceiling and replaying the day. Power.

glosses: An act or instance of replaying (of playing something, such as a game, again); a replaying of (something).

examples.text: One of the features of Diablo that gives it good replay value is the ability to choose from three character types. Each has its own strengths and weaknesses, thus requiring different strategies and tactics.
It's a no-frills, no-hype game that's not only original in concept but fun to play while providing massive replay value.
I've been in many meetings in which the publishers wanted widely branching stories – the kind that allow (and encourage) multiple replays of the game.

glosses: A repeat or subsequent playing of some or all of something which was previously broadcast or performed, or a playing of something which was recorded, such as a live event or a television broadcast, the gameplay of a computer game, etc.

examples.text: He met Luis Suarez's cross at the far post, only for Chelsea keeper Petr Cech to show brilliant reflexes to deflect his header on to the bar. Carroll turned away to lead Liverpool's insistent protests that the ball had crossed the line but referee Phil Dowd and assistant referee Andrew Garratt waved play on, with even a succession of replays proving inconclusive.
A more common use of such replays is on reality television, where we often are shown earlier scenes and moments to refresh our memories of previous events and to heighten the dramatic stakes.
Of course, what I'm remembering at this point are my own endless replays, and there's no way of knowing whether they've altered subtly over the years.

glosses: A (video or audio) recording of an action or event that is or can be replayed after being recorded; saved video footage (which is, or can be, replayed) of the gameplay of a computer game, a (portion of a) televised sports match, etc.

examples.text: Show us that replay one more time.
The game stores a player's progress on the cartridge and will even automatically save replays of memorable shots.
When you watch a replay, a time meter appears at the bottom of the screen to show you how far you are into your replay.

glosses: A replayed match, often after the first game or match ended in a draw; a rematch.

examples.text: As late as 1971 he was still chasing silverware, helping Real reach the European Cup-Winners' Cup final where they were beaten in a replay by a Peter Osgood goal for Chelsea.

glosses: A repetition of another event, scene, or occurrence; a recurrence or reenactment.

examples.text: Lucia is now the wealthy wife of a well-known orchestra conductor, but like Max she is irresistibly drawn into a replay of their intense liasison, with tragic consequences.
A series about two single, late-30-to early-40-something sisters begins with a replay of the balcony scene from Romeo and Juliet.
But Level 5 is a replay with a subtle twist, resetting the plot of Hiroshima mon amour in the context of the events at Okinawa that preceded the catastrophe of Hiroshima.

glosses: The process of revising:
The action or process of reviewing, editing and amending.

examples.text: Revision can turn a passable paper into an excellent one and change an excellent one into a radiant one.

glosses: The process of revising:
The action or process of reviewing something previously learned, especially one′s notes in preparation for a test or examination.

examples.text: All that last minute revision really paid off in the exam! I got top marks!

glosses: A changed edition, or new version; a modification.

examples.text: The first thing members need to understand about a revision is that the current bylaws are not under consideration at all. If the revision is defeated, no changes to the current bylaws take place.

glosses: To provide with a new vision.

examples.text: What philosophy needs is to be revisioned with a more hopeful, engaged inspirational point of view.

glosses: A second or subsequent reading of a text or artifact in an attempt to gain new insights.

examples.text: I need to make a review of the book before I can understand it.

glosses: An account intended as a critical evaluation of a text or a piece of work.

examples.text: The newspaper review was full of praise for the play.

glosses: A judicial reassessment of a case or an event.

examples.text: The victims demanded a full judicial review of the case.

glosses: A stage show made up of topical sketches etc.

examples.text: The Cambridge Footlights Review launched many Monty Python faces.

glosses: A survey of the available items or material.

examples.text: The magazine contained a review of Paris restaurants.

glosses: A review article.
A periodical which makes a survey of the arts or some other field.

examples.text: The Times Literary Review is published in London.

glosses: A military inspection or display for the benefit of superiors or VIPs.

examples.text: The troops assembled for a review by the Queen.

glosses: A forensic inspection to assess compliance with regulations or some code.

examples.text: The regulators demanded a review against NYSE practices.

The decision to place a young child in group home care is usually done after much review, but it is done more readily if there is substantial reason to believe that a resource-rich and structured program will result in a more speedy reunification or prompt adoption.

glosses: To survey; to look broadly over.

examples.text: Before I tackle the question directly, I must briefly review historical approaches to the problem.

glosses: To write a critical evaluation of a new art work etc.; to write a review.

examples.text: The critic reviews every new play in London.
[…] "The Interview," a crude and poorly reviewed comedy about a C.I.A. effort to hire two bumbling journalists to knock off Kim Jong-un, the North Korean leader […]

glosses: To look back over in order to correct or edit; to revise.

examples.text: "Keith Williams is reviewing his review," the source said. "The whole structure of the industry has changed since he wrote his report. [...]"
